subject: SLA sizing & ops checklist — AcmeHealth dedicated pool follow-up
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.l@redwoodinference.com>
To: Linda Hayes <linda.hayes@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SLA sizing & ops checklist — AcmeHealth dedicated pool follow-up

Hi Linda,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the clear rundown of AcmeHealth's latency sensitivity and the regulatory constraints around PHI. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we all have the same frame: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Primary pain: inference latency spikes during morning batch windows (08:00–11:00 PT) causing timeouts in clinical triage flows.
- Goal: deliver p95 latency <= 200ms for standard text-generation requests, and predictable tail performance for long-form reports (up to 4k tokens).
- Compliance: data residency requirement for PHI (US-only), and audit log retention for 24 months.

Capacity & isolation notes
- Recommended starting footprint: 8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs to support peak concurrent inference and KV cache needs (estimate details attached).
- Isolation preference: single-tenant private pool (VPC) with optional burst to a shared Dedicated lane for non-PHI workloads.

SLA targets and ops
- Proposed SLA: 99.9% availability for GPU pool, operational SLOs for per-request latency p95 <= 200ms; fallback policy to a slightly lower-cost model variant on degraded nodes.
- Monitoring: token-level cost dashboards, per-route latency heatmaps, and an alert for queueing >100ms average for >5m.

Attachments I shared
- Draft MAP (mutual action plan) that maps milestones, procurement owners, and dates.
- SLA target matrix with sizing assumptions.

Next steps (owners & deadlines)
1) Jasmine: send this recap, MAP, and SLA matrix — TODAY (attached).
2) Linda / Procurement: confirm procurement cadence and PO timing — by Wed 7/8.
3) Ben & Rishi: review technical sizing and provide an ops-runbook (including failover play) — by Fri 7/10.

Questions for you
- Is the PHI workload completely segregated from non-PHI pipelines today (networking + storage)?
- Do you have a preferred procurement template or PO cadence that we should align to?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up if you want to walk the MAP line-by-line.

Best,

Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jasmine.l@redwoodinference.com]
[attachment: Draft-MAP-AcmeHealth.pdf (2 pages)]

From: Linda Hayes <linda.hayes@acmehealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.l@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA sizing & ops checklist — AcmeHealth dedicated pool follow-up

Hi Jasmine — thanks for the thorough recap. Confirming a few things and adding procurement context so we can keep momentum.

Quick confirms
- PHI path: yes, PHI pipelines are logically separated today (separate VPCs and S3 buckets with restricted access). We would need Redwood's private deployment (VPC) to meet our audit controls.
- Latency: the 200ms p95 target sounds right for the clinical triage API — longer reports are lower priority but still need predictable tails.

Procurement items
- We use a standard PO process (Net30) and have a draft contract with standard BAAs and data processing addenda. I'll loop in procurement (copied).
- Can you provide a high-level cost estimate for the recommended 8-GPU reserved pool (monthly) and an example of burst pricing to shared Dedicated lanes? We need this for our internal budget review.

Scheduling
- Procurement will aim to issue an initial PO in the next 2–3 weeks if the pricing is in line with expectations.

Thanks — attaching a short checklist our legal team wants to see in any vendor SLA.

—Linda
Linda Hayes
SVP, Operations | AcmeHealth
[linda.hayes@acmehealth.com]
[attachment: Acme_SLA_Checklist.pdf (1 page)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Linda Hayes <linda.hayes@acmehealth.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.l@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA sizing & ops checklist — AcmeHealth dedicated pool follow-up

Hi Linda — appreciate the checklist and clarity on the PHI separation. A few technical clarifications plus concrete sizing/cost-high-level so your procurement team has what they need.

Quick clarifications (from our infra scoping)
- Workload mix: our sizing assumes ~60% short generative calls (avg 80 tokens) and ~40% long-report generation (avg 2.5k tokens) during peak. If your mix differs by >15%, call this out and we'll re-run.
- KV cache: to meet the p95 tail targets for long reports we recommend a warm KV cache layer with sticky routing — increases effective throughput by ~25%.

Proposed starting config & cost (ballpark)
- Reserved pool: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (private VPC) — estimated monthly commitment: $68,000/month.
- Burst: up to +4 GPUs on shared dedicated lanes at $X/hour (we'll provide exact burst rates in the pricing sheet).
- One-time onboarding & runbook creation (ops playbook + canary plan): $12,500.

SLA and fallback
- SLA proposal: 99.9% availability for the reserved pool; additional operational SLOs: p95 latency <= 200ms, mean queue wait < 50ms.
- Fallback behaviour: on degraded nodes we can route PHI requests to the private pool only; non-PHI can fail over to a compatible quantized variant in the shared lane.

Ops deliverables (owner / ETA)
- Ben: Ops runbook + failover play (includes run commands, monitoring thresholds, escalation path) — target 2026-07-10.
- Jasmine: Updated MAP and pricing sheet for procurement — target 2026-07-08.
- Rishi: Finalized sizing assumptions + cost sensitivity matrix — target 2026-07-09.

Action items for AcmeHealth
- Procurement: confirm PO cadence and whether Net30 is acceptable to Redwood.
- Ops: share traffic mix if possible (hourly breakdown) so we can tune batching windows.

I'm attaching the SLA-Target-Matrix we referenced and a short example MAP. Happy to jump on a 30-minute technical sync with your infra lead if needed.

Thanks,

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Inference Ops | Redwood Inference
[rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com]
[attachment: SLA-Target-Matrix.xlsx (3 sheets)]
